items.title: Section: The Sixth Angle Opens — All Ten Powers Attained at Once, Yet Manifesting One by One

items.zh: 云何如來十力次第？謂諸如來，於其無上正等菩提初證得時，即便頓得一切十力；頓證得已，後時次第方現在前。謂諸如來初成佛時，先起處非處智力。觀察諸法，建立一切無倒因果。既觀察已。次起自業智力。若有希求即於欲界同分界中可愛殊勝異熟果者，方便為說令其遠離諸不善業，令其現行所有善業。次起靜慮、解脫、等持、等至智力。若諸有情希求世間離欲法者，與其教授，令彼趣向世間離欲，令彼獲得如實之道。
items.en:
Sixth, sequence; first, posing the question. What is the sequence of the Tathāgata's ten powers?
Second, explaining; first, stating overall. At the moment the Tathāgatas first attain unsurpassed, perfect awakening, all ten powers are attained instantaneously and at once; having been thus attained, they subsequently manifest one by one in sequence.
Second, showing individually; first, the first gateway; first, distinguishing; first, the power of wisdom regarding what is possible and impossible. When the Tathāgatas first become buddhas, the power of wisdom regarding what is possible and impossible arises first, observing every phenomenon and establishing every undistorted cause and effect.
Second, the power of wisdom regarding karma. Having observed thus, the power of wisdom regarding karma arises next: for one who wishes for a desirable, superior ripened result within the same portion of the desire realm, [the Buddha] skilfully teaches that being to abandon unwholesome deeds and bring forth wholesome ones.
Third, the power of wisdom regarding meditative absorptions, liberations, equipoise, and attainment. Next arises the power regarding these; for one who wishes for the worldly dharma of freedom from desire, [the Buddha] instructs that being to progress towards such freedom and attain the path of genuine realisation.

items.title: Section: The Remaining Six Powers in Sequence — From Reading a Practitioner's Faculties to the Final Cure for Spiritual Pride

items.zh: 次起所餘如來七力。若諸有情希求出世離欲法者，如應為說趣出世間離欲之道。謂於此中，先起根勝劣智力，如實觀察希求出世離欲者根。次起種種勝解智力，如實觀察彼根為先所有意樂。次起種種界智力，如實觀察意樂為先所有隨眠。如是了知彼根、意樂及隨眠已，次起遍趣行智力，如其所應，令於所緣趣入門中而得趣入。次起宿住隨念智力及死生智力，彼由如應所緣趣入門加行攝住心已，淨修行已，為說中道，令其遠離薩迦耶見以為根本常斷邊執。為令永斷一切煩惱，從此後起漏盡智力。若有如是正修方便奢摩他力之所任持，雖未永斷一切煩惱，而由獲得不現行故，起不作作增上慢者，令其捨離此增上慢。
items.en:
Fourth, the remaining powers; first, stating overall. Next arise the remaining powers; for beings who wish for the transcendent dharma of freedom from desire, [the Buddha] teaches, as is fitting, the path of transcendent freedom from desire.
Second, explaining; first, the power regarding superior and inferior faculties. Among these, the power regarding superior and inferior faculties arises first, truly observing the faculties of one who seeks transcendent freedom from desire.
Second, the power regarding various resolute inclinations. Next arises the power regarding resolute inclinations, truly observing, on the basis of that faculty, whatever resolute inclination is held.
Third, the power regarding various elements. Next arises the power regarding elements, truly observing, on the basis of that inclination, whatever latent tendency underlies it.
Fourth, the power regarding paths to every destination. Having thus known the faculty, inclination, and latent tendency, the power regarding paths to every destination arises next, causing the being, as is fitting, to enter the corresponding gateway of practice.
Fifth, the powers recollecting past abodes and regarding death and rebirth. Next arise, together, the power recollecting past abodes and the power regarding death and rebirth: once the being has settled the mind through the corresponding gateway of practice and purified that practice, [the Buddha] teaches the middle way, causing the being to abandon the extremes of eternalism and nihilism rooted in the view of self.
Sixth, the power regarding the exhaustion of outflows. In order to bring about the permanent severing of all affliction, the power regarding the exhaustion of outflows arises thereafter. Even one sustained by properly cultivated calming meditation, whose afflictions, though not permanently severed, do not manifest, may fall into an over-estimation of having accomplished what is not yet done; this causes such a one to abandon that over-estimation.

items.title: Section: Two Further Gateways on Sequence — Finding No Teacher Left in All the World, and Compassion Moving the Buddha to Teach

items.zh: 是名十力一門次第。復有異門十力次第。謂諸如來，於其無上正等菩提初證得時，最初發起處非處智力令現在前，普於一切緣生法中，觀察最勝妙法住智。即依如是妙法住智，次起自業智力，觀在家分，由彼彼業種種差別，依在家分曾當現時修證差別。如是觀察在家分已，次起靜慮、解脫、等持、等至智力，觀出家分。謂於如是出家分中，為有能說出苦離苦正道者耶？為無有耶？如是觀已，正知都無。觀諸世間無有救護，無所歸依。由大悲故，以其佛眼如實觀照一切世間。既觀照已，次起根勝劣智力，現前了知住在世間種種有情，生在世間、長在世間，或有鈍根、或有中根、或有利根。現前知已，便於說法其心趣入。次後如前一切所餘種種勝解智力等事，次第應知。是第二門十力次第。
items.en:
Second, concluding. This is called one gateway on the sequence of the ten powers.
Second, the second gateway; first, stating. There is also another gateway for the sequence of the ten powers.
Second, explaining; first, distinguishing the first four; first, the power regarding what is possible and impossible. When the Tathāgatas first attain unsurpassed, perfect awakening, they first bring forth the power regarding what is possible and impossible, manifesting the most excellent wisdom of abiding in the dharma throughout every dependently arisen phenomenon.
Second, the power regarding karma. Relying on this excellent wisdom of abiding in the dharma, the power regarding karma arises next, observing householders — by whatever distinct deeds they perform, what portion of realisation they attain, past, future, and present, in correspondence with being a householder.
Third, the power regarding meditative absorptions, liberations, equipoise, and attainment; first, observing the path of renunciation. Having thus observed householders, the power regarding meditative absorptions arises next, observing renunciates: among renunciates, is there one capable of teaching the true path out of suffering, or is there not?
Second, surveying the world. Having observed thus, he knows with certainty there is none. Seeing the world without protector, without refuge, moved by great compassion, he surveys the entire world with his buddha-eye exactly as it truly is.
Fourth, the power regarding superior and inferior faculties. Having surveyed thus, the power regarding faculties arises next, directly perceiving that beings dwelling in the world, born and raised there, have faculties dull, middling, or sharp. Having directly known this, he teaches the dharma, and their minds enter into it.
Second, extending to the remaining six. Thereafter, as before, all the remaining powers, such as the power regarding resolute inclinations and so forth, arise in sequence accordingly.
Third, concluding. This is the second gateway on the sequence of the ten powers.

items.title: Section: The Third Gateway — From the Dharma-Realm Itself to Beings Who Exist Only as a Name, and the Three Gateways Compared

items.zh: 復有異門十力次第。謂諸如來於其無上正等菩提初證得時，最初發起處非處智力令現在前，觀察一切緣生法界。次起自業智力，即於如是緣生法中，觀察假立有情名想諸有情界，如是有情自造如是色類諸業，還受如是色類諸果。如實觀察如是法界有情界已，次起靜慮、解脫、等持、等至智力，即為如是諸有情類解脫苦故，示現三種無倒神變而教授之。既教授已，次起餘力，如前次第知根等已，於其正道令趣入已，然後方便令彼有情解脫眾苦。是第三門十力次第。
items.en:
Third, the third gateway; first, stating. There is also another gateway for the sequence of the ten powers.
Second, explaining; first, distinguishing the first three; first, the power regarding what is possible and impossible. When the Tathāgatas first attain unsurpassed, perfect awakening, they first bring forth the power regarding what is possible and impossible, observing every dependently arisen dharma-realm.
Second, the power regarding karma. Next arises the power regarding karma, observing, within this dependently arisen realm, the realm of beings provisionally established by name and notion — such beings performing their own distinct deeds and, in turn, experiencing their own distinct fruits.
Third, the power regarding meditative absorptions, liberations, equipoise, and attainment. Having truly observed both the dharma-realm and the realm of beings, the power regarding meditative absorptions arises next; precisely in order to liberate such beings from suffering, it manifests three kinds of undistorted miraculous transformation to teach them.
Second, extending to the remaining seven. Having taught thus, the remaining powers arise next, as before — knowing faculties and so forth — leading them into the true path, and thereafter, through skilful means, bringing about their liberation from suffering.
Third, concluding. This is the third gateway on the sequence of the ten powers.

blocks.text: All ten powers are attained at once, yet they show themselves in order. The treatise gives three ways to understand the order.

"All ten are attained at once, then manifest in sequence." Master Cháng Bǎi: in one moment all ten are accomplished; in subsequent wisdom they appear in order. Venerable Miào Jìng, on the lower aims: this is doing good with a scattered mind; a tranquil mind goes to the form-realm heavens. Master Cháng Bǎi: abandoning the ten unwholesome deeds, practising the five precepts and ten good deeds.
Venerable Miào Jìng: 界 here covers much, but mainly the seeds of affliction.

subs.head: No teacher in all the world

blocks.text: The second gateway surveys householders, the third renunciants. Master Cháng Bǎi: not one renunciant could teach the true path out of the three realms; compassion moves the Buddha to teach.
Master Cháng Bǎi: it goes directly to named beings, their deeds and fruits. Venerable Miào Jìng: the dharma-realm here means dependently arisen things.
"Attained at once, shown in order." Much of teaching is like this: what one understands whole must be given to others one step at a time.

quiz.q: Are the ten powers attained one by one or all at once?
options: attained at once at awakening, later manifesting in sequence
quiz.why: All ten are attained at once, then manifest in sequence. Master Cháng Bǎi: in one moment all ten are accomplished; in subsequent wisdom they appear in order.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "the same portion of the desire realm"?
options: good done with a scattered mind; a tranquil mind leads to the form realm
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: this is doing good with a scattered mind; a tranquil mind goes to the form-realm heavens. Master Cháng Bǎi: abandoning the ten unwholesome deeds, practising the five precepts and ten good deeds.

quiz.q: The sequence goes faculty, inclination, latency. How do the lectures explain 界 here, given the English "elements"?
options: Miào Jìng: mainly the seeds of affliction; Cháng Bǎi: the kinds of beings' affliction-seeds
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: 界 covers much, but mainly seeds of affliction. Master Cháng Bǎi agrees. "Elements" can mislead.

quiz.q: In the second gateway, whom do the second and third powers survey?
quiz.why: The second surveys householders, the third renunciates. Master Cháng Bǎi: not one renunciate could teach the true path out of the three realms.

quiz.q: How do the second and third gateways differ, per Master Cháng Bǎi, and what is "dharma-realm" per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: second: abiding wisdom, then householders and renunciates; third: directly, beings of name and notion and their karma. Miào Jìng: dharma-realm means dependently arisen things
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the second gateway moves from abiding wisdom to householders and renunciates; the third goes directly to named beings, their deeds and fruits. Venerable Miào Jìng: the dharma-realm here is dependently arisen things.
